content:
Mysterium Cooperative Detective Game puts the board game Mysterium at the center of a ghost story, with one player as a silent spirit and up to six others as psychics trying to solve a long past murder using only picture clues and discussion.

How Mysterium Sets Up Its Seance Mystery

In Mysterium, players gather at Warwick Manor after a brutal crime that took place thirty years earlier, and the ghost of a murdered servant tries to guide psychic investigators toward the truth through dreamlike visions represented by illustrated cards.Publisher Libellud describes this cooperative game of deduction and teamwork for two to seven players, with an average play time of 45 minutes and a minimum recommended age of 10. The game targets family and adult groups that can handle a mix of eerie theme and logical reasoning, using an asymmetrical structure where all players either win or lose together when the seance ends.

One player takes on the role of the ghost and cannot speak during play, instead selecting and handing out vision cards that feature surreal artwork meant to hint at suspects, locations, and murder weapons without direct explanation.The official rules emphasize that Mysterium is a cooperative game in which all players share victory or defeat, with the ghost guiding mediums via illustrated vision cards over a fixed number of rounds. The other players act as mediums, interpreting these images and placing their intuition tokens on character, location, and object cards they believe match the ghost's intentions, progressing through the investigation as they guess correctly.

Components And Game Structure For US Players

The boxed game comes with a substantial set of components that support its investigation structure and its communication constraints between ghost and mediums.A detailed US retailer listing specifies 6 intuition tokens, 6 sleeves, 6 clairvoyance level markers, 36 clairvoyance tokens, a clock board, 4 progress boards, 18 character psychic cards, 18 location psychic cards, 18 object psychic cards, a sand timer, 18 character ghost cards, 18 location ghost cards, 18 object ghost cards, 6 ghost tokens, 84 vision cards, 6 culprit tokens, 3 crow markers, a clairvoyance track and a rulebook. The component count reflects the need to track each medium's progress, manage time pressure and handle the ghost's limited communication channels.

Play is structured over a week of in-game nights, usually represented by seven rounds, during which the ghost must help each medium identify a personal combination of suspect, location and object before a final shared vision decides whether the group can reconstruct the full crime scenario.An independent review explains that Mysterium plays out over seven rounds, with mediums receiving one to several vision cards each round to identify a suspect, place and object, before using a final vision to vote on the correct crime scenario. The standard player count band of 2-7 and playing time of about 42-45 minutes makes the game suitable for typical game nights where a single scenario can be completed without stretching into multiple hours.

Brand, Ownership And US Distribution Context

Mysterium is credited to designers Oleksandr Nevskiy and Oleg Sidorenko, and its modern edition is published by French studio Libellud, which focuses on visually driven family and hobby games.Background sources identify Mysterium as a cooperative board game designed by Nevskiy and Sidorenko, with Libellud as the publisher and a player range of 2-7, an age range of 10 and up, and a playing time of roughly 42 minutes. Libellud specializes in titles like Dixit and other games that blend distinct art styles with accessible rules and imaginative themes, positioning Mysterium within a catalog aimed at families and mixed-experience game groups.

Libellud joined the Asmodee Group in 2020, integrating its catalog of games such as Dixit and Mysterium into a larger international distribution network while keeping its own editorial vision.Libellud publicly announced that after years of collaboration, it was integrated into the Asmodee Group, with Asmodee distributing Libellud games in more than 35 countries while Libellud maintained its editorial guidelines. For US readers, Mysterium is sold and distributed through Asmodee's North American operations, using the Libellud brand on the box but relying on Asmodee's logistics and retail partnerships to reach hobby stores and online channels.

How Gameplay Compares To Other Cooperative Board Games

Mysterium sits alongside other cooperative deduction titles but distinguishes itself through its reliance on abstract art and a strict communication barrier between the ghost and the mediums.One review lists a typical price of $54.99 in the US, a player count of 2-7, an age recommendation of 10+, a play length of about 42 minutes and classifies the game as cooperative with low to moderate complexity. That price level places Mysterium in the midrange band for modern hobby board games with substantial component counts, making it comparable in cost to other narrative-heavy titles rather than small card games.

Mechanically, Mysterium is often described as a blend of Clue-style deduction with Dixit-style image association, combining suspect-location-weapon logic with subjective interpretation of art.Coverage of the game highlights its cooperative deduction design with 2-7 players, recommended age 10+, and a playing time of about 45 minutes, noting that one player acts as a silent ghost using large image cards while 1-6 spiritists interpret visions to find the suspect, location and weapon. Compared with many other cooperative games where all players share information freely, the ghost's enforced silence and the abstract nature of the clues introduce uncertainty and tension, which some groups enjoy while others may prefer more structured hint systems.

Against more straightforward cooperative titles that rely heavily on numerical tracks or explicit text instructions, Mysterium leans on the table's ability to discuss and debate symbolism and associative connections, which can make its 42-45 minute sessions feel dense with conversation even though the rules remain relatively simple.Asmodee's description of the Mysterium range emphasizes that the game reinvents investigation and cooperative formats, using asymmetrical roles of Psychic and ghost to create a social experience centered on guessing what other players have in mind. For US players deciding between Mysterium and other cooperative offerings, the key differences lie in its central vision card system, shared win-lose condition and relatively short, self-contained scenario length.

Use Cases, Limits And Who Mysterium Suits Best

Mysterium Cooperative Detective Game works best for groups that enjoy interpreting art and talking through possibilities, making it a strong fit for family game nights with older children and adults who can manage light horror themes and abstract symbolism in a roughly 45 minute session.The refreshed 2025 edition keeps the player count at 3-7, the minimum recommended age at 10 and the average play time at 45 minutes, reinforcing the game's positioning as a one-evening cooperative deduction experience. It is less suited to very young children because its imagery revolves around murder investigation, and its gameplay expects players to handle open-ended clues rather than simple roll-and-move actions.

Groups that prefer highly mechanical or competitive games might find Mysterium's reliance on discussion and artistic interpretation less satisfying than titles with more direct scoring systems, while players who appreciate social deduction and storytelling can lean into the ghost's visions and the mediums' shared attempt to piece together the crime scene.A product-focused article characterizes Mysterium as an atmospheric cooperative deduction board game for 2-7 players aged 10 and up, with a typical game duration of about 40-45 minutes and a focus on jointly solving an old murder over seven rounds through image interpretation. For US readers looking for a game where everyone shares a single success or failure condition and where communication is mostly about deciphering pictures rather than managing resources, Mysterium stands out as a visually rich choice.

Key Facts About Mysterium Cooperative Detective Game

  • Product: Mysterium Cooperative Detective Game board game, standard edition
  • Manufacturer: Asmodee North America (publisher Libellud, part of Asmodee Group)
  • Category: Cooperative deduction board game
  • Players: 2-7 players, recommended age 10+
  • Playing time: Approximately 42-45 minutes per session
  • Components: 84 vision cards, 18 character ghost cards, 18 location ghost cards, 18 object ghost cards, 6 intuition tokens, 36 clairvoyance tokens and additional boards and markers
  • Price: Around $54.99 in the US (as of 09/08/2026)
  • Target audience: Families and adult groups seeking a thematic cooperative mystery game with visual clue interpretation
